subject.title: Reply-session init conflict is silently dropped on Slack/webchat/heartbeat inbound, though Telegram already treats it as retryable

question: Should this issue be resolved by the shared fenced reply-session-init self-heal in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101920, or should maintainers require explicit retry/coalescing parity for WebChat, heartbeat, Discord, and other non-spooled inbound paths?
rationale: The source shows both a shared session-init conflict throw and surface-level terminalization paths; the latest comment provides transient-drop evidence that may not be fully covered by the permanent-wedge PR.

options.title: Review Shared Self-Heal Then Verify Parity
options.body: Treat the open shared self-heal PR as the first fix path, but keep this issue open until WebChat/heartbeat/Discord transient drops are proven fixed or a narrower follow-up is opened.

options.title: Require Surface Retry Parity First
options.body: Ask for explicit retry or coalescing at the unprotected inbound surfaces before accepting the shared self-heal as sufficient for this report.

options.title: Split A Narrow Follow-Up
options.body: Land or reject the permanent-wedge PR independently and create a dedicated follow-up for transient distinct-message conflict drops if they remain.

recommendation.title: Review Shared Self-Heal Then Verify Parity
recommendation.body: Treat the open shared self-heal PR as the first fix path, but keep this issue open until WebChat/heartbeat/Discord transient drops are proven fixed or a narrower follow-up is opened.

likelyOwner.reason: jalehman has the strongest history on the guarded reply-session initialization boundary where this owner-boundary decision sits.
